lead: A standing case can pin the error *class* a refusal arrives in, so a member whose classification you change fails `nv verify`'s conformance leg and not its unit tests.
body: The case's own reasoning paragraph is why it pinned the class, and it can be true and beside the point — `Core\Time::parse`'s zonal-pattern refusal was argued into `ParseError` that way. Read the reasoning before reclassifying, and if it is what is wrong, rewrite that paragraph rather than the expectation alone.
